One person's trash is your fortune.

You step off the boat onto the island town of Çamlıada with empty pockets and one goal: find value where everyone else sees garbage. Dumpster Diving Simulator is a first person scavenging, junk flipping and life sim where every bin might hide a broken toaster... or a collectible worth a small fortune.

Dig Through the Town

  • Real trash piles: rummage through dumpsters and bins all over the island. Every district has its own loot: electronics, hardware, office junk, motel leftovers and neighborhood treasures.
  • Rarity system: common scrap, rare finds and legendary pieces, each with its own reveal moment.
  • Collectibles: rated up to five stars, their true value hidden until an expert appraises them. Sell them to the collector or complete your own collection.
  • Trash Day: once a week the town throws out more, rarer loot than usual. Be ready.

Carry, Load, Haul

  • Physics carrying: lift heavy items by hand, rotate them, drop them or toss them.
  • Pockets and backpack: keep small items in your pocket hotbar and upgrade your backpack to carry more.
  • Truck beds and trailers: stack your finds in the cargo bed, hook a trailer to your ATV or push a hand cart around town.

Many Ways to Make Money

  • Scrap yard and weighbridge: weigh your vehicle, dump your load, weigh again and get paid by material and weight.
  • Scrap price exchange: metal prices change every day. Track them on your laptop.
  • Online marketplace: photograph items with your phone camera, post listings and haggle with buyers.
  • Storage auctions: scan the QR code on a locker door, join the live bidding and.
  • Flea market stall: rent your own stall, set your prices, watch customers line up and bargain face to face.
  • Used car trading: buy cheap cars, haggle, deliver and resell them for profit t
  • Jobs and quests: cleanups, deliveries, scrap jobs, lost item hunts and favors for neighbors, some of them in story chains.

Go Live and Build an Audience

Stream your dumpster dives on Twixel, the in game streaming platform. Find something amazing on camera, build hype, gain followers and earn donations from your fans. The better the find, the louder the chat.

Wheels for Every Job

  • Buy vehicles: browse the gallery app, pick from pickups, vans, wagons, coupes and an ATV and have it delivered.
  • Restore a forgotten pickup: find an abandoned truck in an old barn, clean it, tires and bring it back to life.
  • Realistic upkeep: fuel, damage, working headlights and signals. Run out of gas and call a tow truck from your phone.
  • Paint shop: give your ride a fresh color.
  • Living roads: traffic and pedestrians fill the streets of Çamlıada.

Life on the Island

  • Needs: hunger, fatigue and health. Eat snacks, rest and visit the pharmacy bef
  • A place to live: rent a trailer home or a motel room.
  • Bills and taxes: the town hall sends weekly bills. Pay on time or face the con
  • Banking: use your card at ATMs, track every transaction and take out a loan from AdaBank when times are tough.
  • Shops: buy tools, gear and gadgets at the hardware store, the computer shop an you faster, a headlamp lights up night dives, coveralls keep you clean.
  • Day and night cycle: shops open and close, street lights turn on, and the town feels different after dark.
  • Weekly events: every day of the week has its own rhythm, with special events a

Your Phone and Laptop

Your phone holds the map, camera, photo gallery, marketplace, auctions, tow service and has its own app store with OtoPazar, the scrap exchange, a casino with seven games ofchance and more. Watch out for spam calls though. The more you hang up, the harder they try.

Crime Doesn't Always Pay

Tempted by that unattended item in someone's yard? You can take it. But stolen goods att closer as your wanted level rises, and the island remembers.

Reputation and Progression

Start with nothing. Every job and smart deal raises your reputation, unlocking better paying work, new opportunities and more of the island. Learn which bins are worth your time, which deals are traps and
which junk is secretly gold.

And More

  • Multiple save slots so you can try different paths.
  • Localized into many languages.

From broke newcomer to island legend. Your fortune is in the trash.

Prepare your run before entering the dungeon

Dungebra is a dark fantasy roguelike deckbuilder where every attempt begins before the first fight. Choose your hero, set up your preparation, equip artifacts, and enter the run with a clear direction for your build.

Each choice changes how you approach the next battles: which cards to prioritize, which effects to combine, and how to turn rewards into a strategy that can survive until the end of the map.

Build your deck during the run

Your deck does not start finished. Throughout the run, you choose rewards, adapt your strategy, and decide which cards deserve a place in your build.

Different cards open different paths: direct damage, effect buildup, resource control, setup for bigger plays, and combinations that become stronger once your deck starts to click.

Turn small choices into an engine

Items and artifacts are not just loose bonuses. They help define the rhythm of the run, reinforce synergies, and can change how your plays resolve.

Finding the right combination between cards, items, artifacts, and hero is at the heart of Dungebra: a strong run is not about one powerful card, but about several pieces working together.

Choose artifacts that change your strategy

Before and during progression, artifacts help give your build an identity. Some support a more aggressive playstyle, while others favor preparation, survival, or effects that grow over time.

The best choice is not always the obvious one: it depends on your hero, your deck, and the direction you are trying to build in that run.

Play with different heroes

Each hero brings a different way to start and plan a run. Your character choice influences your priorities, your risks, and the type of build that makes sense to pursue.

Try different combinations and discover which heroes best match your playstyle.

Unlock, discover, and try again

Dungebra is built around short runs, constant decisions, and that feeling of wanting one more attempt. Even when a run goes wrong, you learn the cards better, understand new combinations, and come back with another build idea.

Choose your destination, face enemies in sequence, improve your strategy between fights, and carry your engine to the final challenge.

Key features

  • Dark fantasy roguelike deckbuilder.

  • Deck built during the run through rewards and choices.

  • Heroes with different preparation styles.

  • Artifacts, items, and cards creating build synergies.

  • Short runs focused on adaptation, strategy, and replayability.

  • Progression through unlocks and new preparation options.

MATCH, MERGE, AND SURVIVE!

Dungeon & Match is a dark fantasy game that blends the addicting comfort of the classic Match-3 genre with the ruthless, tactical depth of Roguelites. Delve into randomly generated dungeons, exploit your enemies' weaknesses, and use your wits to survive.

DEADLY COMBINATIONS (ITEM FUSION)

Merely matching and blasting tiles isn't enough; the items in your inventory dictate your strategy! Create powerful new gear by combining base items:

  • Shield + Staff = Soul Scythe Attacks the enemy's soul. Grants you a shield equal to the damage dealt.

  • Sword + Shield = Spiked Shield Deals physical damage to the enemy equal to your current shield amount.

KEY FEATURES

  • Tactical Match-3 Combat: Every swipe matters. Match swords to attack, armor to defend, and hearts to restore your health.

  • Endless Replayability: Every run offers different enemies, diverse item pools, and new opportunities.

  • Deep Build System: Thanks to roguelite elements, you can use the items you collect to become an untouchable tank or a one-shotting BEAST.

  • Ruthless Bosses: Test your skills against powerful foes who will disrupt your matching tactics and throw their own deadly obstacles onto the board.

Dungeon Buster is an incremental dungeon-building extraction autobattler RPG. Build the dungeon, send in your hero, and turn every successful expedition into permanent power.

Expand a mysterious underground stronghold room by room. The paths you create determine what your hero discovers, which dangers they face, and how deep they can travel before returning with their spoils.

Build. Battle. Extract. Improve.

Your hero explores and fights automatically, using the equipment, spells, potions, and skills you prepared. Watch them clear rooms, overcome traps, collect treasure, and decide whether to continue into the darkness or return safely.

A failed expedition can cost you what you have not secured. A successful extraction brings resources back to the Workshop, where they fuel permanent upgrades and an even larger dungeon.

The Dungeon Is Your Progression

Every room you add creates new routes, encounters, rewards, and risks. Unlock new construction options, discover special rooms, break the Wardens’ seals, and prepare your hero for the Guardian waiting at the dungeon’s heart.

Combine equipment effects, active abilities, passive skills, and permanent upgrades to create increasingly powerful runs and increasingly dangerous opportunities.

Features

  • Build and expand your own interconnected dungeon

  • Automatic exploration and combat

  • Extraction decisions with escalating risk

  • Persistent Gold, XP, skills, and upgrades

  • Equipment, spells, potions, passives, and build combinations

  • Treasure rooms, traps, locked chambers, minibosses, and secrets

  • A growing dungeon map shaped by your choices

  • Multiple Wardens and a final Guardian to overcome

  • About 3-4 hours of incremental gameplay

  • Come find us on Discord to chat or leave feedback!

How deep will you build—and how much will your hero bring back?

An old-school dungeon crawler

Dungeon Cleared! began with a simple idea: I wanted to recreate the feel of 1980s tabletop dungeon crawlers and the rules of 1990s role-playing games, without conversations or lengthy narrative sequences: exploration, combat and tactical decisions, even in short sessions.

The rules are easy to learn, but your decisions matter.

The order in which you move your heroes, who opens a door, where you end your movement and when you use a spell can completely change a fight.

Casual in the time it requires, not in the consequences of your choices.

Three campaigns. Thirty dungeons.

Build a party of four heroes and face three campaigns of ten dungeons each.

In the depths beneath Valdombra, you will search for the fragments of the Solar Seal while the Rift threatens the village.

The Court of Frost leads the party through a frozen realm inhabited by creatures of ice and cold.

In the Garden of Spores, nature has taken on considerably less reassuring forms.

Each campaign features its own setting, enemies, obstacles and bosses, with a major encounter in dungeon five and a final boss in dungeon ten.

Seven classes. Four heroes.

Choose your party from Warrior, Rogue, Wizard, Cleric, Elf, Dwarf and Halfling.

Each class has different stats, movement, range, equipment, spells or abilities.

Your party composition changes the way you approach each room.

Your turn. Your order.

Activate your heroes in any order and combine movement and actions during the same turn.

Move forward, attack and reposition. Cast a spell, use a potion or take advantage of your class power.

Doors, walls and obstacles affect movement and line of sight, while fog of war hides what lies beyond the next room.

From level 1 to level 10

After each dungeon, your party grows stronger.

Choose permanent upgrades, new items and gradually develop your heroes’ abilities.

New spell tiers and additional slots become available throughout the campaign, allowing you to gradually shape the party around your choices.

Procedural dungeons

Maps, traps, obstacles and encounters are generated procedurally, turning each seed into a different tactical situation.

The system is deliberately easy to read: you do not need to manage dozens of overlapping mechanics, only understand how to deal with what is in front of you.

At higher difficulty levels, enemy behaviour also changes, with greater aggression and different priorities when choosing targets.

Campaign or One-shot

Play one of the three complete campaigns or create a level 1–10 One-shot by choosing your party, difficulty and seed.

Four difficulty levels — Easy, Normal, Hard and Hardcore — let you tailor the experience or experiment with new party compositions without starting a new campaign.

The town is dying.

The king fled before dawn. He took the treasury, the guard, and the last reason to hope. What was left were people who still needed to be fed, and nobody came forward.

You are Dormer, assistant to Steward Grimvard. You run the kitchen, the warehouse, and the laboratory. You have thirty days.

Heroes go underground for anything that can go into a pot. They come back with ingredients nobody knows anything about.

Who do you test them on?

A rat answers only one question: safe or not. It will not say how bad. Poison builds up in it after every test, so it needs rest between trials, and a strong enough ingredient simply kills it.

New rats come from corpses. Read that sentence again, because the whole game rests on it. The better you feed the town, the fewer people die. The fewer people die, the fewer rats you have. The fewer rats you have, the more often you face an ingredient you know nothing about.

Then it comes down to a person. A hero, if you can afford to weaken one, or a citizen, who may not survive it. A hero lost in the laboratory will not make the next expedition. A citizen goes on the list of the dead, with a name, a day, and a cause.

You can also skip the test entirely and serve people something you never touched yourself.

The pot has a bottom

You combine two to five ingredients; the safe ones dilute the poisonous. A bigger pot feeds more mouths, but cooking eats hours you do not have.

A dish splits into portions, one per person per meal. The same pot feeds the party below and the town above, so every campfire meal is food taken from somebody upstairs.

Feeding the fed gets you nothing. The portions vanish, no strength returns, and at the first exertion someone brings it all up in a corridor or mid-fight and loses a turn.

The cook grows practiced with ingredients she cooks often. She works faster, but she takes no responsibility for what comes out of the pot.

The town eats at noon and at dusk

You do not hand out meals yourself. The townspeople go to the warehouse on their own, at set hours, and take what you left there. The decision was made earlier, and at that moment you may be underground, two floors down.

Safe food buys another day. Tainted food takes your morale first, then your health, then your life. An empty table kills too, only slower and quieter.

Tainted dishes and deaths lower your reputation, feed the rumors going around town, and are written into the final reckoning. The town remembers what you fed it.

You learn the dungeon over and over

The corridors lay themselves out differently every time. You go down with three picked from six classes. The Torchbearer, the Cartographer, the Rogue, the Herbalist, the Ranger, and the Knight each solve different problems, and there is no lineup that covers everything at once.

How long you stay down is your call. After dark you see less, morale sinks, and the dungeon starts filling with things that were not there in daylight. You can mark your way in your own blood, if you're willing to pay for every rune with the party's health and morale.

A hero pushed without a break starts tripping over their own fatigue, and sleep debt is repaid only on a bunk at the tavern. You have to rotate the party, because sleep debt does not go away on the march.

The game keeps no notes for you

Combat runs on a spinning D10, but this is not classic dice rolling.

The die spins on screen. You decide when to stop it.

Every result is read from the enemy's hidden hit table and can mean a miss, a graze, a full hit, or a critical. Each enemy type has its own layout within a given expedition.

The game will not show you the finished table. It will not fill one in after every attack, and it will not write what you have learned into the bestiary. You see a number and what happened after it.

If you want to truly know an enemy, you watch, you memorize, or you keep your own notes. The way old games made you draw the dungeon map yourself, this one makes you reconstruct the dice.

Within a single expedition that knowledge is yours. You know which numbers to avoid and which are worth stopping on. On the next descent the tables are shuffled again, and old notes stop being the answer.

Heroes have their limits

Low morale ends in panic, refusal to fight, supplies smashed in blind fury, or desertion. Hunger stacked on despair can tip into frenzy, and then, depending on the class, a hero attacks a companion, eats an ingredient they found, or throws themselves at the nearest enemy.

Death is permanent. The rest of the party loses morale, and what the fallen carried stays below, gone for good unless you go back for it before you leave.

The game will not stop the world to shield you from the outcome of one decision.

Power does not ask your permission

Grimvard gives orders and imposes reforms that change the terms of life in town. You do not pick them from a list and you do not get a vote. You are handed new rules and expected to keep working in a world that, with every passing day, looks less like a place that can be saved.

Dungeon Cooking grew out of the old, unforgiving dungeon games, Beneath Apple Manor and Dungeon Campaign. It does not pretend it is still the eighties.

It is a modern game built on an old assumption: your decisions can be wrong, and the game will show you their consequences.

And all it will tell you is how much food is left.

Explore the darkness. Command your allies. Build your legacy.

The war between Chaos and the gods left the world broken.

Kingdoms are collapsing, ancient horrors are awakening, and supernatural forces are spreading across the land. As a warrior marked by tragedy, you must gather allies, uncover forgotten secrets, and build enough power to confront the forces threatening to consume everything.

Dungeon Explorers 2 is a dark fantasy RPG that combines first-person dungeon crawling, tactical battles, party-based combat, faction management, exploration, meaningful choices, and romance in a single evolving adventure.

Enter Deadly First-Person Dungeons

Descend into dangerous labyrinths filled with roaming monsters, hidden passages, deadly traps, powerful enemies, and valuable treasures.

Navigate every corridor carefully, uncover secret rooms, avoid threats you are not prepared to face, or hunt them down for greater rewards.

Every expedition demands preparation, awareness, and courage.

Command Tactical Battles

Lead your warriors across strategic battlefields in turn-based tactical combat.

Position your units, exploit enemy weaknesses, protect vulnerable allies, and use each companion’s abilities to turn impossible battles in your favor.

Your decisions on the battlefield can determine who survives.

Fight Alongside Your Party

Face enemies through a classic front-view battle system built around party composition, equipment, abilities, and teamwork.

Recruit new companions, strengthen your group, unlock new skills, and create a party capable of confronting increasingly dangerous threats.

Build and Manage Your Faction

Your influence extends far beyond the battlefield.

Recruit warriors, guards, gatherers, merchants, and specialists. Send followers on missions, collect resources, protect refugees, respond to emergencies, and decide how your growing faction should operate.

Your companions will offer advice, but every final decision belongs to you.

Make Choices That Matter

Your actions shape your reputation, alliances, relationships, and personal path.

Choose between virtue and ambition. Support rival factions, resolve conflicts, decide who deserves your trust, and face the consequences of every major decision.

Different choices can unlock new opportunities, alter relationships, and change the direction of your journey.

Forge Meaningful Relationships

Meet warriors, merchants, nobles, adventurers, outlaws, and mysterious beings from across the world.

Earn their trust, discover their personal stories, fight beside them, and develop relationships that can grow into lasting romances.

Explore a Dark Fantasy World

Travel through cities, forests, roads, fortresses, refugee settlements, ancient ruins, and forgotten places shaped by war and supernatural forces.

Accept quests, discover hidden events, visit specialized shops, train new abilities, acquire powerful equipment, and encounter characters with their own goals, loyalties, and secrets.

Create the Warrior You Want to Become

Your choices define your journey.

Develop your abilities, customize your equipment, recruit the companions you trust, and decide what kind of leader you will become.

Will you protect those who cannot defend themselves, pursue power at any cost, or carve out a path between both extremes?

Challenge Chaos Itself

Ancient churches, ambitious nobles, legendary warriors, forgotten gods, and servants of Chaos are all fighting for control of a wounded world.

Build your faction.

Strengthen your allies.

Uncover the truth.

And prepare to challenge forces far greater than yourself.

The world is falling into darkness.

Your journey begins now.

Dungeon Miner is a 1–4 player co-op mining game about heading down into the mine, digging up ore, and carrying it back to the ship in your own two arms.

Gear up aboard the ship and descend into a mine that's generated fresh every run. Small gear like your pickaxe and flashlight stays on your body, but the huge ore you dig out doesn't fit in any inventory. You have to pick it up and carry it yourself.




Swing your pickaxe at a vein and crystals come tumbling out. The bigger and rarer they are, the more they're worth, but the moment you wrap both arms around a big one, you can't use your pickaxe or a weapon. When something closes in through the dark, the crystal in your arms is both a precious haul and an awkward burden.




No damage numbers, no health bar. Get caught once and that's it. In exchange, every threat gives you a warning first: a sound, a light, a movement. Whatever a fallen teammate dropped, the rest of the crew can pick up and bring home. Spend what you've cashed in to recruit a new miner, and they'll join you on the next run.




The cart is a handcart you pile things onto. It's slow, and if it tips, your ore spills out. Lay down rails and run a rail cart instead and it's faster and leaves your hands free, but it takes an investment.




Once you've gathered enough ore, pull the Dungeon Core at the very bottom. The moment you do, the mine starts to collapse and a three-minute countdown begins. Everything hiding in the dark bursts out at once and comes after you. Abandon the cart and run, or hold on a little longer for the ore? That call decides whether this run pays off. Only what you throw into the ship's intake counts as money, and the Dungeon Core becomes fuel for the next voyage.




The mine is built fresh every run. Straight, man-made tunnels and winding natural caves join up at random into a tight, tangled maze, and you won't know where the veins are, or what's lurking where, until you go down. Pick the size of your next mine at the ship's CRT terminal. The bigger and deeper it is, the bigger the payout, and the bigger the danger.


Your base is a ship docked deep inside a tunnel. Buy gear with what you've earned, pick the next mine, and head back down. Dig your way deep on your own at your own pace, or take on a mining run with a crew of up to four.
